macros.name: calccentering
macros.doc: After calling \calccentering, ⟨length⟩ is the amount to be added to the margin to center the textblock.

macros.name: cancelthanksrule
macros.doc: Issuing the command \cancelthanksrule will cause the normal \footnoterule definition to be used from thereon; another \usethanksrule command can be issued later if you want to swap back again.

macros.name: droptitle
macros.doc: You can change the vertical position of the title via the length \droptitle.

macros.name: emptythanks
macros.doc: The \emptythanks command discards any text from prior use of \thanks.

macros.name: makethanksmarkhook
macros.doc: A vacuous macro used as a hook into \makethanksmark.

macros.name: thanksfootextra
macros.doc: \thanksfootextra{⟨pre⟩}{⟨post⟩} inserts ⟨pre⟩ and ⟨post⟩ before and after the thanks markers in the footnotes.

macros.name: thanksgap
macros.doc: Use the \thanksgap{⟨length⟩} command immediately after a mid-line \thanks or \thanksmark command to add ⟨length⟩ amount of space before the next word.

macros.name: thanksheadextra
macros.doc: The \thanksheadextra{⟨pre⟩}{⟨post⟩} command will insert ⟨pre⟩ and ⟨post⟩ before and after the thanks markers in the titling block.

macros.name: thanksmargin
macros.doc: The value of the length \thanksmargin controls the indentation the second and subsequent lines of the thanks text, with respect to the end of the mark box.

macros.name: thanksmark
macros.doc: The command \thanksmark{⟨n⟩} is similar to \footnotemark[⟨n⟩] in that it prints a thanks mark identical to that of the ⟨n⟩’th \thanks command.

macros.name: thanksmarkseries
macros.doc: The command \thanksmarkseries{⟨format⟩} command can be used to change the marking style.

macros.name: thanksmarkwidth
macros.doc: The thanks mark in the footnote is typeset right justified in a box of width \thanksmarkwidth.

macros.name: thanksscript
macros.doc: \thanksscript typesets its argument as a superscript, which is the default for thanks notes.

macros.name: theauthor
macros.doc: The package provides the \thetitle, \theauthor and \thedate commands that can be used for printing these elements of the title later in the document, if desired.
